thread.title: Tech Today: Red Hat Plunges, Cheers for Micron, Apple Loves to Fight Patents

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Red Hat Plunges, Cheers for Micron, Apple Loves to Fight Patents
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Red Hat fails to meet high expectations
Shares of Linux and open-source software distributor Red Hat ( RHT ) are down $20.39, or over 12%, at $145.34, after the company yesterday afternoon reported fiscal Q1 revenue and profit that topped analysts' expectations, but also forecast this quarter's results lower and cut its outlook for this year's revenue.
The cut in outlook, the company said, was solely to account for the rise in exchange rates , which lower the company's dollar-denominated results. In addition to the cut in outlook, the company's " billings " number, $709 million, came up short of the consensus $721 million.
There are a number of price target cuts this morning, and there's at least one downgrade, from BTIG's Joel Fishbein , who cuts his rating to Neutral from Buy. "Perhaps the most perplexing part of the print," writes Fishbein, "is how quickly sentiment has shifted in the past month since Analyst Day ." The company had "raved about momentum with new products," he observes, but now things seem a bit less enthusiastic.
"With limited visibility, we are left wondering if this speed bump doesn't warn of more to come," he writes, noting that a lot is "baked into" the back half of this year, "potentially creating a tough situation if 2Q doesn't go as planned."
The forecast for the full year now calls for $3.38 billion to $3.41 billion, down from Red Hat's prior forecast of $3.43 billion to $3.46 billion, and also lower than the average Street estimate for $3.45 billion.
The company also said its board approved a new $1 billion share-repurchase plan to replace the previous $1 billion plan, of which about three-quarters had been spent.
As the Intel turns
Bloomberg News Analysts continue to mull the ouster yesterday of Intel ( INTC ) CEO Brian Krzanich after he was found to have violated the company's policy against romantic involvements by managers with staff.
Most analysts seem to be adjusting to the sudden announcement. But one bull on Intel shares is somewhat more concerned about Krzanich's departure.
Quinn Bolton of Needham & Co . reiterates a Buy rating today, but he also cuts his price target to $60 from $62, writing that Krzanich "was the driving force behind Intel's transition to a data centric business."
He's concerned what happens next without Krzanich at the helm.
"With Advanced Micro Devices ' ( AMD ) EPYC processor positioned to take server market share, DCG [Intel's Data Center Group, the server-chip unit] facing much tougher comps beginning 4Q18 and persistent 10nm manufacturing issues, we believe the level of risk to Intel's shares has increased," Bolton writes.
Pierre Ferragu of the boutique New Street Research , who has a Buy on the shares, ponders who the next CEO could be. He acknowledges it could be an inside candidate but also that there's a prospect of an outside hire .
His first choice is Chief Financial Officer Bob Swan , who is taking over in a temporary fashion, Intel said. Swan is an outsider, and "he should have a strong bias towards rationalizing operations and the portfolio," writes Ferragu.
In terms of a truly outside candidate, he would like to see VMware ( VMW ) CEO Pat Gelsinger . "On paper, the ideal candidate: a great business track record as CEO of VMWare and as technologist as CTO of Intel. Pat is both an'outsider' and a 30-years Intel veteran."
Intel stock this morning is up 85 cents, or 1.6%, at $53.04.
BlackBerry falls on Q1 report
BlackBerry ( BB ) shares are down $1, or almost 9%, at $10.70, despite the company reporting this morning fiscal Q1 revenue and earnings that topped analysts' expectations, and forecasting this year's software growth higher than what the Street has been modeling.
CEO John Chen said the company was "off to a solid start." He said he was "pleased" with the fact that "BlackBerry QNX software is now embedded in over 120 million automobiles worldwide, doubling the install base in the last three years."
"We are very excited about the opportunities ahead of us in automobiles and in other EoT verticals."
Revenue in the three months ended in May rose 11%, year over year, to $217 million, yielding EPS of 3 cents. That compares to consensus for $210 million and break-even on the profit line.
BlackBerry ended the quarter with $2.3 billion in cash.
For the full year, the company expects its billings will rise by "double digits," it said, and it said its software and services revenue will rise by 8% to 10%. That's a little better than the 8% that the Street has so far been modeling.
More praise for Micron
Shares of memory-chip giant Micron Technology (MU) are down 53 cents, or 1%, at $58.90, despite the stock getting an initiation at a Buy recommendation by Mike Burton with the Benchmark Group this morning, with an $80 price target:
Writes Burton, "We believe MU has progressed from a'cash burn' to a'cash return' story in only 2 years, and we expect the stock to remain a cyclical growth name, generating increasing profits and cash flow on each respective high and low of the memory cycle."
He bases his Buy on three things: "little evidence of a supply glut in MU's DRAM business heading into 2H18 (or until significant wafers are added due to structural tightness)," with four generations of product set to follow its current DRAM; NAND chips where "MU has become a cost leader at 64-layer 3D NAND"; and Micron beginning to "use its FCF to buy back stock in FY19 after becoming net cash positive in the May quarter."
Burton's initiation follows Micron's upbeat earnings report Wednesday , which had prompted multiple price-target increases yesterday .
KLA-Tencor is not a place for investors to hide
Shares of chip equipment maker KLA-Tencor (KLAC) are down $3.33, or 3%, at $106.98, after Needham's Edwin Mok this morning cut his rating on the shares to Hold from Buy, after concluding, based on his "checks," that there is "increased risk" that customers in the " foundry " business-meaning contract chip manufacturers such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM)-will spend at a slower than expected rate for tools to make chips with 7-nanometer or 5-nanometer feature sizes.
"We think this is similar to CY15, when foundries delayed 16nm/10nm investments and KLAC stock came under pressure," writes Mok.
He notes KLA stock has done better this year than have competitors Applied Materials (AMAT) and Lam Research (LRCX). That's because the latter two have greater exposure to memory-chip makers, where there has been concerns about a slowdown in spending on tools. But KLA is not immune to those concerns, he writes:
"With the recent increased chatter on memory pushouts, we believe investors are'hiding' in KLAC on its relatively lower exposure to memory than of its peers.
"However, we believe DRAM has been a big contributing factor in the growth of memory," Mok opines, and the "recent news" that Samsung Electronics ( 005930KS ) is "pushing out" some of its DRAM production, he argues, "will negatively impact KLAC's CY3Q18 shipments, similar to how it will negatively affect AMAT and LRCX."
Mok maintains a Buy rating on Lam shares and a Strong Buy on Applied.
Apple loves to invalidate patents
Apple (AAPL) is making vigorous use of the patent system, according to an interesting piece this morning by Susan Decker of Bloomberg .
Decker notes that in Apple's ongoing legal battle with Qualcomm (QCOM), the company has requested that the U.S. Patent Office invalidate four patents that Qualcomm last year accused Apple of infringing. Those include things such as Qualcomm's claim on "a device that functions as both a phone and a personal digital assistant."
Decker writes that "Apple is one of the most aggressive users of the proceedings at the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, which has an easier legal standard than courts do, and frequently seeks to invalidate patents when it's been sued for infringement."
"The iPhone maker has filed 398 petitions challenging patents, according to the patent office's electronic database," writes Decker.
Apple stock this morning is up 17 cents at $185.63.
